content: Over recent years, ICASA has focused on restructuring these frameworks to better align with industry needs, ensuring that licensees can operate within a predictable and streamlined regulatory environment. Historically, between 2020 and 2023, significant regulatory changes were introduced in the form of adjustments to the ECNS and ECS licence frameworks. The primary objective during this period was to improve compliance and streamline operations for telecom providers across the country. These historical adjustments laid the groundwork for a more robust administrative process, aiming to reduce bureaucratic bottlenecks and provide clearer guidelines for market entrants and established operators alike. By clarifying the operational scopes of network services and communications services, the regulatory authority sought to foster a more competitive telecommunications sector, which is critical for driving broadband expansion and improving connectivity for South African consumers. Building upon these earlier reforms, ICASA has continued to evaluate the efficacy of its licensing structures. In late 2025, the authority announced the initiation of a public inquiry specifically targeted at potential adjustments to the framework governing Individual ECNS (I-ECNS) and Individual ECS (I-ECS) licenses [95] . This move signaled a strong willingness on the part of the regulator to revise existing policies to meet contemporary industry demands and address any lingering operational frictions. Leading up to this inquiry, the scale of the licensing ecosystem was substantial. As of November 2025, ICASA reported that it had issued a total of 470 I-ECNS licenses and 458 I-ECS licenses. Furthermore, the authority had approved 171 transfers of ownership and control, providing a clear snapshot of high license activity and active regulatory engagement preceding the outcomes of the public inquiry [95] . This volume of licensing activity underscores the dynamic nature of the South African telecommunications market and the critical role that Vcom and its competitors play in shaping the sector's infrastructure. Despite the proactive steps taken in late 2025, the regulatory landscape as of June 2026 presents certain ambiguities. Information regarding the finalized outcomes or definitive updates stemming from the public inquiry remains largely absent, leaving a degree of uncertainty regarding the immediate future of the I-ECNS and I-ECS regulatory frameworks [95] .
